Export an Imported PEtab Problem

Source: R/PEtabInterface.R
exportPEtabObject.Rd

Writes a problem returned by importPEtab() back to PEtab: the parameter, observable, condition and measurement tables, for v2 also the experiment table, the SBML model and a YAML file. Conditions the importer split are merged again. For a problem built in dMod, use exportPEtab().

Usage

exportPEtabObject(
  petab,
  dir,
  modelID = NULL,
  formatVersion = "2.0.0",
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

petab

A petabproblem returned by importPEtab(), or a list with the same components.

dir

Output directory, created if missing.

modelID

SBML model identifier. Default NULL: the model id of the imported problem, else "dMod_export".

formatVersion

"2.0.0" (default) or "1".

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE (default), existing files in dir are an error.

Value

Path to the written YAML file, invisibly.

Details

Limits:

  • Parameter scales are read from attr(petab$bestfit, "petab_scales"); without it they are "lin".

  • v2 has no parameter scales: values and bounds are written on the linear scale, with a warning.

  • v2 has no priors on the parameter scale: such a prior is written as the matching prior of the linear parameter, with a warning.

  • v1 has no experiment periods, no start time other than 0 and fewer prior distributions: periods and later starts are an error, a prior without a v1 form gives a warning.

  • v2 has no log10 observable transformation: it is written as "log-normal" noise, with a warning.

  • Initial values set per condition only in the parameter transformation are not written to a v2 condition table; use formatVersion = "1" to keep them.

  • SBML <algebraicRule> elements are not imported and therefore not written.

See also

importPEtab(), exportPEtab()

Examples

# \donttest{
yaml <- system.file("extdata/petab_boehm/Boehm.yaml", package = "dMod2")
petab <- importPEtab(yaml, backend = "cppDE", cores = 1, outdir = tempdir())
#> Sparse Jacobian detected (8x8, 21 nnz, 67.188% sparse)
#> Sparse Jacobian detected (8x8, 21 nnz, 67.188% sparse)
#> using C++ compiler: g++
#>   every source : -O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -DKLU -I/usr/include/suitesparse
#>   2 of 5 also  : -DKLUBTF=0 -DKLUAMD=0 -fopenmp
petab
#> <PEtab problem Boehm>
#>   source:        /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/dMod2/extdata/petab_boehm/Boehm.yaml
#>   conditions:    1 (1 sim, 0 preeq)
#>   observables:   pSTAT5A_rel, pSTAT5B_rel, rSTAT5A_rel
#>   measurements:  48
#>   bestfit (n=9): Epo_degradation_BaF3, k_exp_hetero, k_exp_homo, k_imp_hetero, k_imp_homo, k_phos, sd_pSTAT5A_rel, sd_pSTAT5B_rel, sd_rSTAT5A_rel
#>   fixed   (n=4): ratio, specC17, cyt, nuc

# The objective at the nominal values
petab$obj(petab$bestfit)$value
#> [1] 276.4441

# The prediction needs the fixed parameters
fixed <- attr(petab, "petab_meta")$fixed
times <- seq(0, 240, length.out = 61)
plot(petab$prd(times, c(petab$bestfit, fixed)), petab$dataList)


# Write the problem back to PEtab
yamlOut <- exportPEtabObject(petab, file.path(tempdir(), "boehm"),
                             formatVersion = "1")
readPEtabTables(yamlOut)$parameters
#>             parameterId parameterScale lowerBound upperBound nominalValue
#> 1  Epo_degradation_BaF3          log10      1e-05      1e+05 2.698251e-02

#> 9        sd_rSTAT5A_rel          log10      1e-05      1e+05 3.152713e+00
